text: Writing clean code is like writing a clear letter to your future self. The most important rule is to make your code readable, not just for the computer, but for other humans. This starts with good naming conventions: a variable called userAge is much clearer than x, and a function named calculateTotalPrice tells you exactly what it does. Instead of writing one long, confusing block, you should break your work into small, focused functions, each with a single job. This makes testing easier and helps you avoid repeating the same logic. Ultimately, the goal is maintainability. When you or a teammate returns to the code after six months, good structure means you can understand and change it without stress or fear of breaking something.
